text:
alex: noticing a spike of 502/526 errors for the eu-west endpoints since ~09:12UTC, looks TLS related, tagging eng-sre

riley: saw the alerts, dashboards show ALB 5xx up across two target groups. any client examples?

alex: curl from my laptop fails with: 
```
curl -v https://app.eu-west.redwood-inference.example --resolve app.eu-west.redwood-inference.example:443:52.23.88.12
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_finished:wrong signature type
```

maria: interesting — ops noticed a pattern: services that use alternate TLS port (8443) for internal probes are healthy, but same host on 443 gets cert for the default app domain instead of the customer-mounted cert. could be SNI mismatch when ALB forwards to ingress on different port.

sanjay: ALB config: we use host-based listener rules on 443 with SNI routing to target groups. The ingress controller (nginx-ingress) is terminating TLS on port 443 for some pods and we also have a sidecar doing mTLS on 8443 — maybe listener prioritized by port not SNI?

jo: I reproduced: when pod has both 443 and 8443 listeners, ALB health/connection reuse sometimes picks the wrong TLS cert chain (served by default host cert) for client requests that set SNI to the customer hostname. Happens intermittently.

alex: could be TCP connection pooling at ALB reusing backend connection that was established for a different SNI/port combo and then forwarding a new request with different SNI. backend expects SNI per connection when doing TLS passthrough -> mismatch.

maria: config snippet from problematic ingress: 
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTP":80},{"HTTPS":443}]'
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: "HTTPS"
spec:
  rules:
  - host: customer-a.eu-west.redwood-inference.example
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        backend:
          service:
            name: customer-a-svc
            port:
              number: 8443
```
Note the port mismatch: ALB sends to 443 but backend expects 8443 mTLS.

sanjay: that annotation is wrong; we had historic migrations where internal probes stayed on 8443. but ALB level connection reuse can indeed cross-request reuse. ALB is doing TLS termination for listener rules when certificate is attached, but we also use TLS passthrough for some flows -> messy.

riley: what's the immediate impact? user-facing traffic sees intermittent TLS failures when the reused connection serves wrong cert. Some customers hit it more because they have long-lived connections.

certbot: Automated cert rotation triggered for customer-a yesterday at 02:05UTC — new cert provisioned to ingress, but ALB cached old cert in one target group's listener for a short window (replica drift). I can confirm certs are in sync now.

alex: mitigation options? 1) make ALB create separate target groups per port+host to avoid pooling; 2) switch to TLS passthrough to backend (NLB) for these customer-hosted cert flows; 3) change probes to use same port 443 and align protocols.

jo: quick, low-risk change: update health checks to use 443 everywhere and ensure backend protocol is HTTPS. That should reduce mismatched backend connections.

sanjay: agree; we'll patch ingress annotation and rollout yesterday's nginx-ingress fix that disables connection reuse for TLS backends (there's a flag to set "proxy_ssl_session_reuse off;").

maria: action items:
- sanjay: update ingress for affected customers to point probes at 443 (oncall ticket created)
- alex: add ALB rule audit to detect host->port ambiguity and report any host with mixed backend ports
- riley: schedule canary to switch one shard to NLB passthrough for high-risk customers to compare error rates
- jo: prepare a rollback plan if TLS regressions surface during rollout

alex: I'll also add a short message for Support to communicate to impacted customers (apology + ETA).

riley: timeline? can we push the health-check change in the next 30m?

sanjay: yes, I'll push a small k8s patch; watching deploy-bot for rollout status.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: ingress-config-patch by sanjay on eu-west cluster. Pods rolling: 3/3 -> 0/3 -> 3/3 (simulated)

certbot: Rechecked certs: chain order is valid; no action required on PKI side.

jo: will monitor logs for connection reuse errors and TLS handshake failures; if we still see >1% 5xx on 443 after change, escalate to network kernel team.

maria: thanks all. tentatively closing incident when error rate <0.2% for 1h post-change.

alex: thanks — keeping thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
